name: redb-table-restore
instr:
Please add a way to roll back one table in redb at `/app` without rolling back the rest of the database. Expose these methods with default features:

- `redb::WriteTransaction::restore_table(&mut self, savepoint: &Savepoint, table: impl TableHandle) -> Result<(), SavepointError>`
- `redb::WriteTransaction::restore_multimap_table(&mut self, savepoint: &Savepoint, table: impl MultimapTableHandle) -> Result<(), SavepointError>`

The handle selects a name, not Rust key/value types. Restore that name's definition and original tree from the savepoint, reusing its pages rather than rebuilding entries, so its table statistics match the saved tree. A name absent at the savepoint becomes absent now; a name absent in both places is a successful no-op. Leave other tables and all savepoints alone. In particular, a later whole-database restore must still work with either an older or a newer savepoint. Restored pages must remain live, and replaced pages must be reclaimed without leaks or double frees, through commits, aborts and reopen, for persistent and ephemeral savepoints and either durability setting.

Add the unit variant `redb::SavepointError::TableTypeMismatch` when either the saved or current name has the wrong table kind for the method. Reject a restore with `InvalidSavepoint` if the saved tree shares any pages with another current table, as can happen after a rename. These validation errors leave the transaction usable. Otherwise use the validity, durability and partial-failure p
